ingredientSources.title: Moisturizing and Antiinflammatory Properties of Cosmetic Formulations Containing Centella asiatica Extract
ingredientSources.study: Ratz-Łyko et al., 2016: 25 healthy volunteers; 2.5% and 5% extract creams/gels, twice daily on forearms for four weeks.
ingredientSources.finding: The tested preparations improved hydration and reduced the response to experimentally induced irritation.
ingredientSources.limit: Different extract preparations and concentrations; healthy forearm skin, not an acne or rosacea treatment trial and not a trial of this sunscreen.

ingredientSources.title: Efficacy of cream-based novel formulations of hyaluronic acid of different molecular weights in anti-wrinkle treatment
ingredientSources.study: Pavicic et al., 2011: 76 women; 0.1% HA creams at five molecular weights, twice daily for 60 days, compared with vehicle around the other eye.
ingredientSources.finding: The tested HA creams improved hydration and elasticity; two lower molecular weights also improved wrinkle-depth measurements at day 60.
ingredientSources.limit: Specific creams and known molecular weights; the sunscreen’s HA concentrations and molecular weights are not verified by this study.

ingredientSources.title: Niacinamide: A B vitamin that improves aging facial skin appearance
ingredientSources.study: Bissett et al., 2005: 50 women; randomized, double-blind split-face comparison of 5% niacinamide and vehicle, twice daily for 12 weeks.
ingredientSources.finding: The tested preparation improved several measures of photoaged skin appearance, including fine lines and uneven pigmentation.
ingredientSources.limit: A 5% test preparation, not this sunscreen; its niacinamide concentration and equivalent outcomes cannot be inferred.

ingredientSources.title: The influence of a cream containing 20% glycerin and its vehicle on skin barrier properties
ingredientSources.study: Lodén and Wessman, 2001: 17 healthy volunteers; bilateral, double-blind comparison of 20% glycerin cream and vehicle for ten days.
ingredientSources.finding: Hydration measurements increased with the glycerin cream.
ingredientSources.limit: The study did not show improved water loss or resistance to detergent irritation. Different concentration and finished formula.

ingredientSources.title: Evaluation of anti-wrinkle efficacy of adenosine-containing products using the FOITS technique
ingredientSources.study: Abella, 2006: 126 women aged 45–65; controlled study of a 0.1% adenosine cream or 1% dissolvable film; assessments at three and eight weeks.
ingredientSources.finding: The tested adenosine preparations improved measurements of facial lines.
ingredientSources.limit: Different dose and delivery systems, not this sunscreen; not evidence of a seven-day sunscreen result.
